titleZh: 让公共交通真正方便每一个人

cet4.title: A Better Bus Journey for Everyone
cet4.summary: 一辆新公交车不等于方便的出行。到站、看懂时刻表和上车都是交通服务的一部分，小障碍可能让出行变得困难。

paragraphs.text: A city can buy a modern bus and still leave many passengers with a difficult journey. Reaching the stop, understanding the timetable and finding the right entrance are all parts of public transport. A service becomes useful when these parts work together. Thinking only about the vehicle can hide the small barriers that make an ordinary trip stressful for someone else.
paragraphs.translation: 一辆新公交车不等于方便的出行。到站、看懂时刻表和上车都是交通服务的一部分，小障碍可能让出行变得困难。

paragraphs.text: Imagine a parent travelling with a child, or an older passenger carrying shopping. A clear sign can prevent confusion before the bus arrives. A seat at the stop can make waiting easier. Information that is both visible and spoken can help people who cannot rely on one form alone. These improvements are often described as special assistance, but many passengers may find them useful at different times.
paragraphs.translation: 清楚标识、等候座椅及视听信息能帮助带孩子、提物品或有不同需要的乘客，改善往往不只对某一个群体有用。

paragraphs.text: Reliable information matters as much as physical design. If a service changes, people need to know what to do next. A message that simply announces a delay may not help a passenger choose another route. Staff and journey planners should explain alternatives in clear language. Listening to actual users can reveal problems that are difficult to notice from an office or a map.
paragraphs.translation: 线路变化时，乘客不仅要知道延误，还需要理解可选路线。听取真实使用者的意见，可以发现地图和办公室里看不到的问题。

paragraphs.text: There will always be choices about limited space and money. Improving one stop may be easier than changing a whole network. However, each decision should consider who can use the service and who is left out. A comfortable journey is not merely a faster ride. It is a sequence of understandable steps that allows people to reach work, education and everyday activities with greater confidence.
paragraphs.translation: 预算有限，但每个决定都应考虑谁被服务、谁被排除。舒适出行不只是更快，而是可理解、连贯的步骤与参与日常生活的信心。

paragraphs.text: Small trials can help a city learn before making a wider change. Residents might try new signs at one stop and explain which information remains unclear. The results can guide the next improvement. A trial is most useful when people know what is being tested and can see how their feedback influences the final decision.
paragraphs.translation: 可以先在一个站点试用新标识，听取居民对模糊信息的反馈，再作更广泛改进。说明试验目标和反馈影响会提高试验价值。

options: Only the speed of a vehicle matters.
Passengers should never ask for information.
Every transport problem requires a new bus.
A good transport service considers the whole journey.
questions.explanation: 文章把出行看作互相关联的多个环节。

questions.prompt: Who may benefit from clear signs and suitable waiting spaces?
options: Only tourists buying expensive tickets.
Nobody who has used a bus before.
Passengers with a variety of everyday needs.
Only the people who design the buses.
questions.explanation: 这些措施可以帮助不同条件下的乘客。

questions.prompt: What makes a delay announcement more useful?
options: Using language that only specialists understand.
Explaining realistic alternative ways to travel.
Giving no information about other routes.
Assuming that every passenger knows the area.
questions.explanation: 替代方案能帮助乘客决定下一步。

questions.prompt: Why should planners listen to users?
options: They may notice obstacles that a map does not reveal.
Every user has unlimited money to invest.
Maps can never show any useful information.
Professional knowledge has no role in planning.
questions.explanation: 实际体验可补充专业分析，发现隐蔽问题。

questions.prompt: What is the broader purpose of transport improvement?
options: Making every trip identical in length.
Removing all choices from passengers.
Replacing every public space with a road.
Helping people participate in everyday activities.
questions.explanation: 交通改善的最终目标是支持日常生活的参与。

cet6.title: Accessible Transport Begins with the Whole Journey
cet6.summary: 一辆新公交车不等于方便的出行。到站、看懂时刻表和上车都是交通服务的一部分，小障碍可能让出行变得困难。

paragraphs.text: Public transport is frequently assessed through the vehicles that operate it: their speed, age or source of power. These characteristics matter, but they do not describe the entire experience of travelling. A passenger must reach a stop, obtain usable information, board safely and complete the final part of the journey. A barrier at any stage can undermine the value of improvements elsewhere. Accessibility therefore concerns a connected system rather than a single feature added to a bus.
paragraphs.translation: 交通不能只按车辆速度、车龄或动力来源评价。乘客必须经历到站、获取信息、上车和抵达目的地，各环节的障碍都会削弱其他改进。

paragraphs.text: Considering different passengers makes these connections more visible. A person with limited mobility may need a suitable pavement as well as an accessible entrance. Someone unfamiliar with the area may need information that remains understandable under pressure. Visual and spoken announcements can complement one another when a passenger cannot easily rely on either alone. Although such measures may be associated with particular groups, their usefulness often extends to people carrying luggage, accompanying children or recovering from an injury.
paragraphs.translation: 不同乘客让关联需求更明显。无障碍入口需要合适的人行道，视听播报可以互补，带行李、照顾孩子或暂时受伤的人也会受益。

paragraphs.text: Information becomes particularly important when a service is disrupted. Knowing that a bus is delayed does not automatically tell a traveller whether to wait, walk or change routes. A useful announcement explains realistic alternatives and indicates which parts of the information are uncertain. This reduces the burden placed on passengers to interpret a changing situation independently. It also requires coordination between the people who manage the service and those who communicate with its users.
paragraphs.translation: 发生中断时，只报告延误不足以支持决策。有效沟通需要解释可行替代方案和不确定信息，减少乘客独自解读情况的负担。

paragraphs.text: User involvement can expose obstacles that formal plans overlook. A route may appear convenient on a map while requiring a difficult crossing on the ground. A timetable may be technically accurate yet presented in language that is hard to understand. Observing journeys and inviting specific feedback can therefore complement expert analysis. Consultation should include people who currently avoid the service, because their absence may reflect a barrier rather than a lack of interest in public transport.
paragraphs.translation: 使用者反馈能发现正式规划忽略的障碍。调查也应覆盖没有使用服务的人，他们的缺席可能反映障碍而非缺少兴趣。

paragraphs.text: Budgets inevitably require priorities, and no single project will remove every difficulty. Nevertheless, evaluating choices through the whole journey offers a useful principle. Investment should be judged partly by whether improvements connect to one another and expand meaningful access. A faster vehicle brings limited benefit if a passenger cannot reach or understand the stop. The broader objective is dependable participation in everyday life, with transport serving as a means of access rather than an end in itself.
paragraphs.translation: 预算需要排序，但应从全程考虑投资是否互相衔接、是否扩大真实可达性。交通最终服务于居民参与日常生活。

paragraphs.text: Small trials offer a practical way to improve the system incrementally. Testing revised signs at one stop, for example, can reveal whether the wording answers passengers’ actual questions. The process becomes more credible when organisers explain what they are testing and report how feedback has influenced the next decision. Evaluation should examine unsuccessful journeys as well as smooth ones. Otherwise, the most difficult experiences may remain absent from the evidence used to justify investment.
paragraphs.translation: 小范围试验可逐步改进系统。组织者应说明试验与反馈结果，并关注未能顺利完成的行程，否则最困难的体验可能再次被证据排除。
